sections.title: Positioning
sections.summary: Squarespace sells the website as the foundation of a small business: one product for presence, selling, booking, invoicing and content, wrapped in design credibility.
keyPoints: Homepage: 'A website makes it real', with 'Start for free. No credit card required.'
The jobs listed on the home page are offering services, selling products, invoicing clients, getting booked, collecting donations, monetizing content and showcasing work.
A banner offers 30% off all plans and says when it ends (Nov 23).

sections.title: Products and offerings
sections.summary: A website builder at the center, with commerce, marketing and business tools attached.

rows: Template-based sites, plus an AI website builder
Unlimited products, customizable listing pages, product reviews, shipping and order management
Email and SMS campaigns, SEO tools, banners and promotions, analytics
Scheduling, invoicing, donations, memberships and business email
Tools for selling merchandise drops and exclusive bookings

gaps: Unfold, the social app, and the free tools were not opened.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.summary: Four monthly plans with a 14-day free trial and an annual-billing saving. Transaction fees drop to zero on the second plan, and card rates fall as the plan rises.
keyPoints: The pricing page says free for 14 days and that paying annually saves up to 36%.
All plans include built-in AI tools, secure hosting, unlimited bandwidth and selling functionality.
Basic charges a 2% online store transaction fee; Core and above charge none.
AI credits scale by plan: 10 one-time on Basic, then 20, 40 and 120 a month.

rows: Free custom domain, 2 contributors, 2% online store fee
No store fees, advanced discount and promotion tools, advanced lead capture, automated taxes and shipping, free year of Google Workspace email
Lowest fees, high-traffic checkout, 120 AI credits a month

gaps: Prices shown are annual-billing prices; monthly-billing prices were not captured as text.

sections.title: Merchandising
sections.summary: A plan ladder organised around selling features, with a recommended middle plan and an urgency banner. Merchants get unusually direct merchandising tools, including a reserved cart and countdown timer.
keyPoints: Core is tagged recommended and is where store transaction fees disappear and discount tools unlock.
A pay-annually toggle, a 'save up to 36%' line and a 30% off banner with an end date push toward annual billing.
For merchants: advanced discount and promotion tools, banners and promotions, a reserved cart with countdown timer, customizable listing pages, product reviews and limited-release tools.
Marketing tools sit in the same product: email campaigns, SMS campaigns with a credit system, SEO and social integrations.

sections.title: Technical platform
sections.summary: A developer site offers Commerce APIs, Reseller APIs and a custom-code spec, plus an engineering blog. It is thinner than the developer sites of the payments and subscription companies in this survey.
keyPoints: Developer page: 'Everything you need to build and publish external apps — reliable APIs, clear documentation, and a marketplace.'
It names Commerce APIs, Reseller APIs and a reliable custom code spec, with notifications for API updates and breaking changes.
The engineering blog covers docs-as-code, a write-back cache on Google Cloud Spanner and browser standards work.
gaps: API reference, rate limits and the marketplace were not opened.

sections.title: Design
sections.summary: Design is the product. Full-bleed photography and short, large headlines on a black-and-white system with one blue, shown through live templates.
keyPoints: One typeface (Clarkson) runs across the home page, pricing and developer site, with 4px button corners and a sticky header.
Home opens on a full-bleed photograph with a centered white headline and one white button.
Pricing is plain: a white page, a pay-annually toggle and four cards, with a blue 'Recommended' tag on Core (#0072f0).
The home page is 7,826px tall and carries 12 videos.
For merchants: templates designed to sell, an AI builder, customizable listing pages and drag-and-drop editing.
gaps: Mobile and dark mode were not assessed.

sections.title: Company presentation
sections.summary: A creative-economy story told through templates, customer websites and product news, rather than metrics.
keyPoints: Home: 'Join millions of entrepreneurs who run their business on Squarespace.'
The showcase page lists customer websites with no stories or numbers.
The newsroom leads with tools for selling limited releases and drops.
gaps: No leadership information in the surveyed pages.

signupPath: On the first survey run, 'GET STARTED' on the homepage led to squarespace.com/templates/get-started, a page headed 'What's your site about?' with a topic search, popular topics (Photography, Design, Education, Consulting, Art and more), 'I'M JUST BROWSING' and a NEXT button. It asked for no account details at that step. In later runs the same button did not lead to a new page, so that one observation is not reproduced in the saved capture. Nothing was entered.

jtbd_fit.evidence: The homepage lists eight jobs from selling products to getting booked.

capability_visible.evidence: Templates, plan comparisons and feature pages show a lot; the editor itself is behind signup.

pricing_transparency.evidence: Four plans with prices, card rates, transaction fee and AI credits; monthly-billing prices not captured as text.

product_breadth.evidence: Websites, stores, marketing, scheduling, invoicing, donations and finance each have their own page.

platform_depth.evidence: Commerce and Reseller APIs and a custom-code spec exist, but the developer site is short.

time_to_value.evidence: Capture stops before the product; first-value time was not observed.

friction.evidence: The surveyed pages could not tell.

trust.evidence: 'Millions of entrepreneurs' and a list of customer sites, with no numbers or stories.

mobile.evidence: Phone captures exist for home and pricing but were not assessed.

states.evidence: No error or empty states reached.

value_prop_clarity.evidence: 'A website makes it real' is brief and the subhead and job list explain it.

proof_quality.evidence: Scale is stated without a figure shown in text; an SMS stat carries a footnote.

persuasion_integrity.evidence: A 30% off banner states its end date, but the product also sells a countdown timer to merchants.

cta_logic.evidence: 'GET STARTED' is the one repeated action across pages.

company_narrative.evidence: The hero is generic; the newsroom story (limited releases) is more specific than the homepage.

offer_packaging.evidence: Four plans with a recommended tag, an annual toggle and a clear feature ladder.

offer_architecture.evidence: Free trial, annual discount, a limited-time sale, falling card rates and transaction fees that vanish at Core.

merchant_merch_tools.evidence: Discounts, banners, reserved cart and countdown timer, reviews, listing pages and drops tooling.

visual_craft.evidence: Strong photography and restrained typography; the hero is image-heavy with little product detail.

system_coherence.evidence: Same typeface, button shape and header across marketing, pricing and the developer site.

merchant_design_control.evidence: Templates built to sell, an AI builder and customizable listing pages are the core product.

read.summary: A design-led site builder with a very clear plan ladder tied to selling features, an urgency banner and, unusually, merchandising tools that include a reserved cart and countdown timer. The platform story is thin and the proof is generic.
pros: Plan table shows price, card rate, transaction fee and AI credits side by side.
Transaction fees disappear on the recommended plan, which gives a reason to choose it.
Consistent type, buttons and header across marketing and developer pages.
Merchants get discounting, reserved-cart and drop tools.
cons: Proof is thin: 'millions of entrepreneurs' and a list of sites.
The developer platform is short next to the payment and subscription sites.
The countdown-timer tool and the sale banner both use urgency.
Two of the surveyed pages returned rate-limit errors on the first run.
read.howItSells: Sells craft and ease: a beautiful site in minutes, with a free trial and no card. Backs it with a clear plan ladder and a time-limited discount.
copy: Tie plan upgrades to specific selling features.
State a sale's end date in the banner.
Use one typeface and button shape on every page.
avoid: Generic proof statements with no figures.
Urgency on both the offer and the merchant tools.
unknowns: What the account creation flow asks.

hypothesis.statement: Adding two named customer stories with revenue or booking figures to the pricing page will lift plan starts among visitors who compare plans.
hypothesis.decisionRule: Ship if plan starts rise by a pre-agreed margin and trial-to-paid holds over four weeks.

merchandising.summary: The most sales-feature-driven ladder so far, with tools that let merchants run drops, countdowns and discounts.
pros: Recommended plan is where store fees vanish.
Annual toggle and save line are above the cards.
Merchants get a countdown timer and reserved cart.
cons: Sale banner and countdown tooling lean on urgency.
Monthly prices were not shown in the text.

design.summary: Design is the product and the site demonstrates it, with good consistency across marketing and developer pages.
pros: Full-bleed photography and short headlines look premium.
The same typeface and button shape run through every page.
cons: The hero shows little of the product.
The engineering blog uses a different style from the main site.

claims.text: Free for 14 days. Pay annually to save up to 36%.
Start for free. No credit card required.
